newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Nine killed in Pakistan sectarian shootings.
newsitem.headline: Nine killed in Pakistan sectarian shootings.

text.p: At least nine people were killed in what appeared to be Moslem sectarian shootings on Monday in the central Pakistan province of Punjab, government and Shi'ite Moslem sources said.

Gunmen sprayed bullets in a bazaar in the southern Punjab town of Shorkot, killing at least seven people from the minority Shi'ite sect and one from the majority Sunni sect, a government official in the area said.
In a separate incident, a Sunni lawyer, Mian Mohammad Arshad, was killed by gunmen in the provincial capital Lahore, police said.

No one immediately claimed responsibility for either shooting, but police said the incidents seemed the latest in a wave of tit-for-tat shootings which militant Sunni and Shi'ite groups blame on each other.
Earlier, Shi'ite sources in Islamabad put the death toll in Shorkot at nine, saying all the victims were Shi'ites.

Sectarian violence is rife in Punjab with militant Sunni and Shi'ite factions engaged in a feud that officials say has killed more than 100 people so far this year, including religious scholars, lawyers and doctors.
On Sunday, a Shi'ite activist, Malik Ghulam Sarwar, was shot by three men on motorcycles as he opened his shop at another Punjab town, Chichawatni, 200 km (125 miles) southwest of Lahore.
Sunni groups accuse neighbouring Shi'ite Iran of financing Pakistani Shi'ite militants, while Shi'ites accuse Sunni Saudi Arabia of aiding Sunni groups.

Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan. Shi'ites form about 15 percent of Pakistan's mainly Sunni population of more than 135 million but are the majority in Iran.
